label.en: 🗺 AP Statistics — College Board Exam Weightings

body.en:
UnitTitleExam %Key Topics
U1Exploring Data15–23%Categorical & quantitative variables, distributions, summary stats, normal model
U2Sampling & Experimentation12–15%Sampling methods, experimental design, bias, confounding
U3Probability & Distributions30–40% (U3+U4+U5)Probability rules, geometric & binomial distributions, sampling distributions
U4Statistical Inference25–35%Confidence intervals, significance tests for means & proportions, chi-square, regression

AP Statistics introduces students to the major concepts and tools for collecting, analysing, and drawing conclusions from data. The course follows four interconnected themes: Exploring Data, Sampling and Experimentation, Probability and Distributions, and Statistical Inference.

value.en: Exploring data — graphical displays, measures of centre and spread, bivariate data, linear regression.
Sampling and experimentation — study design, bias, randomisation, experimental control.
Probability — rules, random variables, Normal and Binomial distributions, sampling distributions, CLT.
Inference — confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, chi-square tests, regression inference.

body.en: Exam format: Section I — 40 MCQ (90 min, 50% score). Section II — 6 FRQ (90 min, 50% score): 5 standard FRQs (approx. 12 min each) + 1 Investigative Task (Question 6, approx. 25 min, worth 25% of Section II).

label.en: ⏱ Free Response Strategy & Question 6 Investigative Task

body.en:
• Pacing: Allot 65 minutes for Questions 1–5 (~13 minutes each) and reserve a full 25 minutes for Question 6 (the Investigative Task). Question 6 is worth 25% of your total FRQ section score!
  • Calculator & Formula Sheet: You are provided the official College Board formula sheet and statistical tables (Standard Normal Table and t-Distribution Table). Graphing calculators (TI-84/Nspire/Casio) are permitted throughout the entire exam.
  • Show Statistical Notation: When writing calculator commands (like normalcdf or 1-PropZTest), always write the standard mathematical formula or label your inputs (e.g., lower, upper, mean, SD) to receive full credit if you make a keystroke typo.

label.en: ▲ The 4 Golden Rules of AP Statistics FRQs

body.en:
• 1. Always Interpret in Context: Every definition, slope, intercept, confidence interval, or conclusion MUST include the specific context (variable names, population, units). An answer with perfect numbers but missing context receives only Partial credit ('P').
  • 2. Use Comparative Language: When comparing two distributions, never just list values for each separately. You must explicitly use comparative words: 'The median salary of Group A is greater than the median salary of Group B.'
  • 3. Never 'Accept' the Null Hypothesis: We never prove \(H_0\) is true; we only 'fail to reject \(H_0\)' due to insufficient evidence. Writing 'accept \(H_0\)' is an automatic deduction on AP rubrics.
  • 4. Check All Assumptions & Conditions: Never proceed to an inference calculation without explicitly naming and verifying the Random, 10% (independence), and Normality / Large Counts conditions.

question.en: Section II Free Response lasts 90 minutes total and contains 6 questions: Questions 1–5 (Part A, 75% of section score) and Question 6 (Investigative Task, 25% of section score). If 25 minutes are reserved for Question 6, calculate the average minutes available per question for Questions 1 through 5.

solution.en: \(\text{Time remaining for Questions 1–5} = 90 - 25 = 65\text{ minutes}\). \(\text{Average time per question} = \frac{65}{5} = 13\text{ minutes/question}\).
